acceptanceCriteria: Recognizably belongs to the Gargoyles family and preserves every identity invariant.
Reads specifically as Sentinel, T2, rather than another family form.
Communicates the Wall-Hop Soldier (Soldier) archetype and its battlefield duty.
Preserves coherent load-bearing anatomy, complete limbs, and believable ground contact.
Uses at least two fire construction dimensions without a palette-only or glow-only treatment.
Keeps the attack telegraph and counterplay signal visible at gameplay scale.
Frames one complete featured subject with no crop, labels, UI text, or watermark.
Output remains a candidate until independent approved-review evidence exists; it is never a runtime asset.
anatomyInvariants: Crouched granite body, weathered moss streaks, small bat wings, blunt claws, and clear masonry joints.
Signature mechanic: Mossed Hop: granite legs push from a wall while small bat wings stabilize, never sustain, one blunt-claw landing.
battlefieldDuty: Repeat short wall-to-floor hops that anchor a predictable claw line.
constructionDimensions: Material/structure branches: T1 chipped sandstone, tiny useless wings, perch chip, and crude water-spout throat gain a ceramic heat sink; T2 granite, moss, and small wings gain fuel-set mortar; T3 broad wings, carved relief, and amber seams gain ember channels; T4 marble, bronze, and tracery gain cooling shutters; T5 buttress wings, throne, and attendants gain bounded throne vents.

Motion/process branches: T1 one short perch drop exhausts through the water-spout heat sink; T2 a hop with small wings burns one measured mortar charge; T3 the dive with broad wings opens relief-channel combustion; T4 a tracery aisle cycles smoke through its bronze shutter; T5 each attendant command feeds and cools one throne vent.
counterplay: Cross under the unwinged side and punish the mortar gap at the landing shoulder. Affinity signal: Affinity counterplay branches: T1 the chipped-sandstone perch and tiny wings expose the water-spout heat sink after exhaust; T2 the granite moss line and small-wing hinge expose cooling mortar after the hop; T3 broad wings and amber relief seams expose an ember-channel vent after the dive; T4 marble, bronze, and tracery expose the cooling shutter after an aisle cycle; T5 buttress wings, throne, and attendants expose the commanded throne vent after combustion.
identityInvariants: Squat crouched construction, hunched shoulders, horned beast face, clawed grip, and folded architectural wings remain recognizable.
Sandstone, granite, marble, bronze, mortar, moss, and water staining remain discrete built materials rather than flesh.
Relief carving, water-spout mouths, restrained amber seams, and pedestal fragments preserve the architectural source grammar.
Stone quality and wing architecture escalate from useless carved flaps to sovereign buttresses while load-bearing joints stay readable.
telegraph: Weathered moss squeezes from one shoulder and the matching small wing unfolds halfway.
